title: [The Bone Crypt] I built a domino-based roguelite deckbuilder using AI for art/music and vibe coded the logic. I have 97 keys left for playtesters!
author: t-squaredGaming
selftext:
Hey everyone,
​I’m a solo dev building The Bone Crypt, a roguelite deckbuilder that completely replaces cards with dominoes. The inspiration actually started from thinking about how I used to play "bones" (dominoes) with my late grandmother, and I wanted to turn that core matching mechanic into a deep strategy game. You chain pips together to build attacks, trigger status effects, and manage your board layout.


​Because I wanted to focus entirely on building tight mechanics and deep synergies, I used AI tools to generate the art assets, icons, and music. I know a lot of standard gaming subs immediately hate on this, so I wanted to bring it to a community that actually understands the workflow.


​I'm currently looking for players who love strategy games to test the balance and try to completely break the logic I've built. I need help with bug hunting, mechanic suggestions, and brutal, honest feedback.


​What's in this build:
​Classes & Relics: Different starting loadouts (like the Rogue's Loaded Dice) and run-altering items.


​Solo & PvP: A full solo campaign, plus a 1v1 online PvP mode.


​I’m using FirstLook to distribute the Steam keys, and I have 97 spots left. You just need to link a Steam account to claim one instantly.


​👉 [the-bone-crypt.firstlook.gg](http://the-bone-crypt.firstlook.gg)


​Would love to hear your thoughts on the gameplay loop!


​The Vibe-Coding Grind:


​For those curious about the actual workflow, I didn't just type "make me a deckbuilder" into a prompt box and hit enter. Vibe coding a full commercial game from scratch is an absolute grind, but it is a process I am incredibly grateful for. AI tools gave me the power to take a massive dream and actually build it, even without a studio budget or years of traditional syntax training.
​Here is a look at the step-by-step reality of 

Bringing The Bone Crypt to life:


​Phase 1: Getting the Bones to Chain
I started with the absolute bare minimum: the physical and logical connection of the tiles. I prompted the logic to make two dominoes snap together, dropped the code into Notepad++, and tested it. If they didn't chain correctly, I refined the prompt. I refused to move forward until the core domino mechanics were flawless.


​Phase 2: Making Connectors Actually Do Something
Once the chains worked, I started assigning data. I had to dictate how connecting specific pips triggered background traits and effects. Every single tweak to the logic was tested in an iterative conversational loop before I ever allowed myself to add the next layer.


​Phase 3: The Combat Loop (Damage & Death)
Next came the stakes. I translated those connector values into active damage numbers against an enemy. I tested the math. Then, I had to build the logic for the enemy's health pool to actually hit zero and trigger a win state. Breaking the game down into these micro-steps (plan, generate, test, break, refine) was the only way to keep the foundation stable.


​Phase 4: The Massive Expansion
Because the core engine was built so methodically, I could safely scale. I used the exact same testing loop to introduce entirely new systems: unique character classes, specific abilities, the shop economy, run-altering relics, pacing, difficulty curves, and eventually the full 1v1 PvP architecture.


​It is a grueling process of acting as the director, architect, and lead QA tester all at once. But for anyone sitting on a great idea who thinks they lack the traditional talent to make a game: the barrier to entry is gone. It takes patience and a ridiculous amount of testing, but you can absolutely build your dream.

comments.author: orbitope
comments.body: Your process seems very reasonable. I would be interested to understand how you worked on balance. I'm working on a deckbuilder on the side, and am pursuing a simulation/basic bot approach to find which cards are overpowered and which strategies are underpowered, etc.

replies.author: t-squaredGaming
replies.body:
That simulation/bot approach sounds like a great plan, especially for a deckbuilder where the math and card synergies can get pretty overwhelming.

​I actually started out with a similar baseline. Here is roughly how my balancing process broke down:

​The Baseline Simulation: I started by running about 50 simulated runs for each class. My main goal here was just to dial in the general win percentages—trying to keep the win rate low for hard difficulties and high for the easy ones. It was a perfect way to get a functional mathematical foundation.

​The Manual Grind: While the simulation gave me the base, the actual balancing was honestly just a ton of manual playtesting. I had to get in there and manually feel out how the relics, buffs, and skills interacted with each other in a real scenario.

​Building Custom Dev Tools: This was the biggest time-saver for that manual testing phase. I built in specific dev commands so I didn't have to play a full run just to test a late-game build. I highly recommend doing this alongside your bots! Being able to instantly spawn specific runes or cards, advance the floor, or skip straight to the last floor to test scaling was an absolute lifesaver.
​The "Creator Tax": Finally, I had to factor in my own bias. Because I built the game, I inherently know all the optimal plays and mechanic quirks. I worked off the assumption that normal players would lose about 25% more often than I did, and I tweaked the final difficulty around that curve.

​Good luck with your deckbuilder! Let me know when there is a demo and I would love to peep it out!

replies.author: orbitope
replies.body: Thanks for sharing your approach! I think I hit the wall of simulation balancing without manual play as well. It's good to hear that intuition from playing is still the best approach for fine tuning and making decisions. I'll definitely take your advice on the dev tools too

replies.author: t-squaredGaming
replies.body:
Happy to help! You are going to have a great time with dev tools. The first time I skipped straight to the end and spawned in a completely broken, overpowered chain of relics and special bones, just to see if the game crashes, I never looked back.

​Keep it up! You are going to crush it with your deckbuilder!
